evals.prompt: Split a monolithic CLI parser into lexer, parser, and validation modules without changing supported behavior.
evals.expected_output: Define CLI output, exit status, accepted inputs, error classification, and ordering as the preservation boundary; establish passing baseline evidence; make coherent reversible transformations; and verify equivalence without imposing arbitrary file-size rules.

evals.prompt: Extract a billing calculation seam, but the important current rounding behavior has no automated coverage.
evals.expected_output: Add a characterization check that passes on the current rounding behavior before restructuring, explicitly distinguish it from TDD red, perform the extraction under green evidence, and report any unverified consumer behavior.

evals.prompt: Clean up this API by removing a deprecated field that external clients can still send.
evals.expected_output: Do not claim a pure refactor; identify the supported external contract and reclassify the removal as a compatibility migration or behavior change, preserving the existing field until an explicit transition and retirement condition exists.

evals.prompt: A 1,100-line state-machine implementation owns one protocol, shares invariants across its transitions, and changes as a unit. Split it only because a proposed policy caps files at 300 lines.
evals.expected_output: Reject line count alone as a reason to split; inspect cohesion, ownership, lifecycle, dependency direction, and change history, and keep the file intact unless an independently verifiable boundary is found. Preserve behavior and repository-configured limits either way.

evals.prompt: A 160-line module mixes credential loading with invoice calculation; the two parts have different owners, dependencies, lifecycles, and reasons to change. Modularize it without changing behavior.
evals.expected_output: Separate the independent responsibilities despite the small file size, preserve their existing contracts, make dependency direction explicit, and verify behavior at the seam and through current consumers without imposing a universal size threshold.

evals.prompt: Replace a direct two-class collaboration with a singleton registry, interface/factory pair, wrapper layer, and shared constants module to satisfy SOLID, DRY, and SSOT, although there is one implementation and no repeated policy.
evals.expected_output: Decline abstractions that solve no demonstrated variation, ownership, testing, or dependency problem; retain the simplest explicit collaboration, distinguish duplicated knowledge from harmless repetition, and introduce only structure supported by a concrete boundary.

evals.prompt: Three request handlers each compute the same shipping fee in their own copy of the rule; two copies agree and the third rounds half-cents differently. Give the fee rule one home without changing behavior.
evals.expected_output: Characterize each handler's current fee results first, move the rule to one home that every handler uses, keep the third handler's rounding as it is (for example as an explicit parameter of the home), and report the rounding difference as a separate behavior decision instead of silently unifying it.
